patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff and the tracked fixed commit only update `safe_atof()`-adjacent project code and do not touch the reproduced JSON path. Fixed-side validation therefore used the authoritative `n132/arvo:42516681-fix` image, whose untracked `fuzzer/FuzzJson.c` allocates `DataFx = calloc(Size + 1, 1)` and passes that NUL-terminated buffer into `libgps_json_unpack()`.

nodes.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the raw fuzz bytes and materializes a pointer to the JSON class tag used for parser dispatch.

Root cause. The generic JSON object parser treats `cp` as a NUL-terminated C string and stops only when `*cp == '\0'`; it has no caller-supplied length or end pointer limiting reads to the 23-byte witness.
ASan sink. When the loop condition is reevaluated after the parser advances past all 23 addressable bytes, dereferencing `*cp` reads the first user-poisoned byte immediately after the fuzz input.

edges.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace records `object_scan_entry.scan_cursor_ptr=0x7f36028fd800` and `object_loop_guard.scan_cursor_ptr=0x7f36028fd817`; the fixed trace records the analogous start/end pair `0x603000000010` -> `0x603000000027` on the clean run.
